newsitem.title: GERMANY: NO NEED FOR INTEREST RATE CHANGE IN SHORT TERM - TIETMEYER.
newsitem.headline: NO NEED FOR INTEREST RATE CHANGE IN SHORT TERM - TIETMEYER.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said in an interview released on Saturday that he saw no reason in the short term for any change in interest rates.
Asked by the news weekly Der Spiegel whether interest rates had now bottomed out, Tietmeyer replied:
"I didn't say that. I simply don't see any reason in the short term for any change in rates. Of course we will continue to check over the next few months whether rates are appropriate.

"But to take the wind out of the sails of anyone speculating -- who might be playing the other side on Anglo-Saxon markets -- I also see no reason for rates to be raised in the foreseeable future," he said, according to the text of an interview released ahead of publication on Monday.
Tietmeyer rejected the idea that the Bundesbank had hurt growth or jobs with its tight monetary policy.
"We have been exceptionally flexible in the last few years," he said. "We have brought interest rates down without letting inflationary expectations arise."
He dismissed the notion that the tight budget policies being followed in other European Union countries in the run-up to monetary union could choke off growth.
"European monetary policy is stability-orientated, but leaves enough room for growth. Short-term interest rates are at a record low."
